summary.text: Jabari Brisport is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent for District 25 in central Brooklyn, running unopposed in the general election. A former public school math teacher who describes himself as a socialist, he has represented the district since 2021 after an unsuccessful 2017 City Council run, and chairs the Senate Children and Families Committee. According to his campaign website, he is running on universal child care, affordable housing, and opposition to ICE and the Trump administration.

paragraphs.text: Jabari Brisport was born in Bedford-Stuyvesant and raised in Prospect Heights, Brooklyn, and describes himself as the son of an undocumented immigrant; Wikipedia lists his birth date as August 9, 1987, and says he graduated from Poly Prep in Dyker Heights.
He earned a bachelor's degree from New York University in 2009 and a master's degree from Yale University in 2014.
Before his election he worked as a public school math teacher in Crown Heights and was an active member of the United Federation of Teachers.

Brisport was an organizer for same-sex marriage legalization in New York from 2009 to 2011 and an early organizer with the Black Lives Matter movement, where he organized rallies and trained protesters on interacting with police.

After the 2016 election he joined the New York City chapter of Democratic Socialists of America and, according to Wikipedia, became a leader in opposition to private development of the Bedford Union Armory in Crown Heights.
In 2017 he ran for the 35th District of the New York City Council as a Green Party candidate against incumbent Laurie Cumbo and lost, receiving 29% of the vote according to Wikipedia.

Brisport won the June 2020 Democratic primary for the open District 25 Senate seat, vacated by Velmanette Montgomery, over Assemblywoman Tremaine Wright and another candidate, then won the November general election and took office in January 2021; he is described as the first openly gay person of color elected to the New York State Legislature.
He was re-elected in 2022 and 2024, and according to Wikipedia he won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 73% of the vote against Marlon Rice.

He chairs the Senate Committee on Children and Families and is also a member of the Banks; Codes; Housing, Construction and Community Development; Libraries; and Procurement and Contracts committees and the Joint Senate Task Force on Opioids, Addiction & Overdose Prevention.
